unit.title: Radicals, Rational Exponents, and Complex Numbers
unit.shortTitle: Radicals, Rational Exponents, and Complex Numbers
unit.act: Act XI - Reversing powers and enlarging the number system
unit.role: Develop exact root arithmetic, radical equations, extraneous-solution logic, and basic complex arithmetic.
unit.governingQuestion: How do we reverse powers, and what happens when the real numbers are insufficient?
unit.storyArc: General roots and rational exponents express inverse powers. Radical arithmetic creates exact forms, conjugates rationalize denominators, and raising powers solves equations but may introduce candidates. Complex numbers complete quadratic solutions.
outcomes: Rationalize denominators using factors or conjugates.
Solve radical equations and perform basic complex arithmetic.
unit.investigation: Compare reversible and nonreversible algebraic steps and explain exactly where extraneous candidates enter.
unit.mastery: Students preserve domains, simplify exact forms, check radical candidates, and express nonreal quadratic roots correctly.
